indicators.note: 'on board' is the crossword convention for being inside a ship, so the sailor goes within the ship's letters

parts.note: a ship one goes on board is an SS, a steamship
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor takes charge of the crew aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means inside SS, the steamship abbreviation: A TAR goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors who take the leading roles in a film are its headline performers.

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the first word could be arranged another way

parts.note: east is one of the four quarters of the compass, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Remedies might partly liberate someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CURES into RESCU; E (east, a compass quarter) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from danger is to save them.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the ceremonial word wraps round the measure

parts.note: a state occasion is a ceremonial one
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A grand occasion stripped of all restraint, just as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just like!' points at the answer to 1 down beside it: the answer means like stars. 'without' means outside here, so STATE goes round ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Star-shaped things are said to resemble the heavenly bodies of the neighbouring entry.

clue.text: Someone else might show no heart

indicators.note: might show suggests the letters can be shuffled to display a different word

explanation.surface: A heartless person might be someone other than you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might show' rearranges the letters of NO HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: A different person is one more besides those already mentioned.

clue.text: Many get thrown out, and that's very sad

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number
ejected means expelled or thrown out

explanation.surface: Lots of people are evicted and feel miserable about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives D, the Roman numeral 500, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast and gloomy, a dejected person is deeply unhappy.

clue.text: He should be well used to facing work!

definitions.text: He should be well used to facing work!

parts.words: He should be well used to facing work
parts.note: reads as someone hardened to confronting labour, but describes a tradesman who puts a smooth face on walls

explanation.surface: A man ought to be accustomed to confronting hard labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' means applying a surface coat to a wall, not confronting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who coats walls with a smooth finish does facing work every day.

clue.text: Attending the trial, being a witness

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
a testing is a trial of something

explanation.surface: Someone present in court giving evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AT TESTING: present at the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness is to declare formally that something is true.

parts.note: re means concerning or to do with
to ply a skill or trade is to exercise it

explanation.surface: A response concerning physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is something said back.

definitions.meaning: a group of people together, often of workers or criminals

explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish verb for walking or going, and a band of people working together.

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Asking whether one or two armbands are allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of jewellery worn round the wrist encircles the arm.

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a verse is a piece of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinclined towards something, and split in two it gives a line of poetry.

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A goddess enjoying a warm spell.
explanation.walkthrough: HERA was the queen of the Greek gods.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek queen of the gods, wife of Zeus, was a deity.

parts.note: suggests a group outnumbered no more, but means the age at which a person legally comes of age in Britain

explanation.surface: A group that is no longer outnumbered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minority' is the legal state of being under age, not a smaller group.
explanation.definitionFit: British law grants adulthood on that birthday, so the person has reached majority.

clue.text: The odd article is true-to life

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters are put into a strange, different order

explanation.surface: A strange piece of writing turns out to be lifelike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ARTICLE IS; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifelike portrayal is faithful to how things really are.

clue.text: Delayed getting overdrawn, so it's said

indicators.note: getting into, so the delayed word goes inside the overdrawn word

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A payment held up sends the account into overdraft, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: LATE goes inside RED, as one gets into the red.
explanation.definitionFit: A story related is one told or recounted.

definitions.meaning: ... were women who kept alehouses or sold ale
a North American fish of the herring family

explanation.definitionFit: Women who sold ale, and a herring-like American fish.

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters are set out in an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: An offence that struck someone as strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges DID SEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence or wrongdoing is a bad deed.

definitions.meaning: private and personal, as a close secret
as a verb, to suggest indirectly

explanation.definitionFit: Private and personal as an adjective, and to suggest indirectly as a verb.

clue.text: Seen as a fault in the Orient-—and stupid

parts.note: a sin is a moral fault
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Something considered a failing in the East, and foolish too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen as' is a link; 'the Orient' gives E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish behaviour is like that of a donkey.

parts.note: suggests people telling untruths without realising, but means people lying down in slumber

explanation.surface: People who tell fibs without being aware of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' means lying down, not telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Those asleep in bed are lying down and unaware of the world.

clue.text: Advantage makes the aged generally content

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Being older usually brings a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' means contents: the letters are inside 'aged generally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge means having a slight lead.

clue.text: To call for silence would be nonsense

parts.note: sh is the sound made to demand quiet

explanation.surface: Asking for quiet would be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish talk is foolish drivel.

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: Sal is a familiar form of the name Sarah
and means together with

explanation.surface: Sarah is holding a pair of easy shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts AND inside SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An open shoe with straps is light and easy to wear.

clue.text: The place of a man north of the Border

parts.note: a Scot is a man from Scotland, north of the English border

explanation.surface: Where a Scotsman lives.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the English racecourse town famous for its royal race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berkshire town with a famous racecourse is a well-known location.

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a king is a royal person

explanation.surface: Imperious, in the way a monarch would be.
explanation.definitionFit: Requesting or requiring something is seeking it.

clue.text: Having no feeling, snubs men clumsily

indicators.note: clumsily suggests the letters are handled badly and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rudely ignores men without any emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' rearranges SNUBS MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of sensation is an absence of feeling.

parts.note: reads as having done excellent work, but describes covering a roof or wall with slabs

explanation.surface: Someone did a splendid piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' is old British slang for excellent, but here it means putting a covering on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering a roof with slates is putting a top on it.

clue.text: Mixed it in a riot he started

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: He jumbled things up and kicked off a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges IT IN A RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who began something is its originator.
